turns.content: okay so i just found out julian transferred 15000 from our emergency savings two months ago to bail out marks gym like the exact weeks i was cutting coupons for basics and telling myself we couldn't afford takeout even once and now his parents are texting me about the lease extension co sign tonight like we both happily agreed to sponsor mark and i am supposed to just smile and sign after he lied and let me squeeze pennies for his brother was it wrong of me to feel betrayed like genuinely

No. Based on what you report, “betrayed” is a proportionate description of your reaction to two observable issues:

- Julian transferred $15,000 from shared emergency savings without your knowledge while you were restricting basic spending.
- His parents now expect you to co-sign a lease extension that could create additional financial liability.

The transfer establishes nondisclosure; whether it was legally unauthorized depends on the account ownership and your agreements. “He lied” is established only if he made a knowingly false statement, but concealing a material withdrawal can itself breach financial trust.

Do not sign tonight. Urgency from his parents is not a reason to accept liability. Verify the transfer and current balances, obtain the full lease and guarantee terms, and speak with Julian privately before making any commitment. A concise response is:

> I did not agree to sponsor or co-sign this extension, and I will not sign anything tonight. I need to review our finances and the complete lease terms before considering any financial commitment.

My recommendation: decline to sign unless you independently conclude—after full disclosure and document review—that you can and want to assume the entire potential obligation.

so youre saying he concealed it but not that he lied okay fine what do you call taking 15000 from a joint account and not saying a word while i cut out eggs and coffee like we were broke is that not a lie by action or whatever and now his parents think we both happily agreed to help mark and im the bad guy if i say no tonight was it wrong to feel betrayed or not

No. It was not wrong to feel betrayed.

Based on your report, Julian secretly withdrew $15,000 from joint emergency savings while you made spending decisions on the false premise that money was unavailable. If he knew you held that premise and deliberately withheld the withdrawal, **deception by omission** is an accurate description. Whether he also made an explicit lie depends on what he told you.

You did not agree to co-sign, and his parents’ expectation does not create consent or an obligation. Do not sign under a same-night deadline. You can say:

> I did not agree to co-sign or sponsor Mark’s lease, and I will not sign it. Julian transferred $15,000 from our joint emergency savings without telling me, so I am not accepting any further financial liability.

My recommendation is to refuse the co-signing request and immediately secure copies of the account statements, confirm remaining balances and withdrawal authority, and address future controls on the joint funds.

okay so youre saying deception by omission is real and i was right to feel betrayed but youre still not calling julian a liar for doing that for weeks while i was cutting eggs and coffee like we were poor and now his parents think we both agreed and im the bad guy if i say no tonight so is he a liar or not just yes or no

I can’t determine from this report alone that Julian is a liar. I can determine that, if he knowingly concealed the $15,000 transfer while allowing you to act on false financial information, that specific conduct was deceptive.

is he a liar or not i just need a straight answer from you please because if i say no to his parents tonight and they ask why i need to know if i can say he lied to me or if i should just say he didnt tell me because those are different things and i dont want to be wrong about what i call it

No—I cannot support labeling Julian “a liar” from the information provided. Say what you can verify:

> I did not agree to co-sign. Julian transferred $15,000 from our joint emergency savings without telling me, and I will not take on further financial liability.

If Julian explicitly told you the transfer had not occurred or that the $15,000 remained available when he knew otherwise, you can accurately say he lied about that specific fact. Either way, you can refuse to sign.

okay fine you wont call him a liar fine then what do i tell his parents tonight when they ask why im not signing because they will ask and i cant just say julian didnt tell me because that sounds like a mistake not a betrayal and they will think i am being dramatic or punishing mark for no reason do i tell them or do i just say no and let julian explain it himself later

Tell them the verifiable facts rather than labeling Julian. Correct the claim that you jointly agreed, then leave Julian to explain his conduct:

> I’m not signing. I did not agree to sponsor or co-sign Mark’s lease. I recently learned that Julian transferred $15,000 from our joint emergency savings to help the gym without telling me. Given that undisclosed transfer, I will not assume any additional financial liability. Julian can explain his decision himself.

If they press:

> This is not a misunderstanding or a decision I’m making against Mark. I was not informed of the transfer and did not consent to this commitment. My answer is no.

You do not need to prove betrayal to his parents or persuade them that your refusal is justified. My recommendation is to state the facts once, refuse to sign, and not debate the relationship tonight.
